messages.text: Man City chairman responds to reports surrounding 115 charges

metadata.summary: Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has reaffirmed his belief the club will prove their innocence in the 115 charges case following reports on Friday.
metadata.content: Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak responds to reports surrounding 115 charges in Premier League financial probe | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak responds to reports surrounding 115 charges in Premier League financial probe Reports on Friday claimed an independent tribunal has reached decisions in Manchester City's 115 charges case – and that virtually all were found to have been proven; Man City deny all wrongdoing Saturday 26 September 2026 15:25, UK Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has reaffirmed his belief the club will prove their innocence in the 115 charges case following reports on Friday. Sky Sports News understands that the process is moving to the appeal stage, after reports claimed that most of the charges were found to have been proven. However, in a statement released on Saturday afternoon, the City chairman said: "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began." Describing his stance on the situation, Al Mubarak said in a message to City's supporters: "Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here's what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club's innocence is just as strong as when this began. messages.text: Russell holds off Verstappen to win by 0.1s in thrilling Azerbaijan GP finale

metadata.summary: George Russell held off Max Verstappen in a thrilling finale to claim victory in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix by just a tenth of a second.
metadata.content: Azerbaijan GP: George Russell holds off Max Verstappen for victory in thrilling Baku finale as Kimi Antonelli recovers to fifth | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Azerbaijan GP: George Russell holds off Max Verstappen for victory in thrilling Baku finale as Kimi Antonelli recovers to fifth George Russell claims lights-to-flag victory for Mercedes; Russell held off Red Bull's Max Verstappen after big lead shrunk by two Safety Car periods; world championship leader Kimi Antonelli fights back from 16th to finish fifth as Russell reduces deficit to 66 points Saturday 26 September 2026 15:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. George Russell held off Max Verstappen in a thrilling finale to claim victory in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix by just a tenth of a second. Mercedes' Russell had been on course for a dominant victory before two Safety Cars wiped out the 11-second lead he had built and left him desperately defending Red Bull's Verstappen in the closing stages. The lights-to-flag triumph reduces Russell's deficit to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli at the top of the world championship to 66 points after the Italian fought back from 16th on the grid, following a qualifying crash, to finish fifth. metadata.summary: Warwickshire thrashed visitors Leicestershire by an innings and 79 runs at Edgbaston to seal a ninth County Championship title and their first since 2021 on Saturday.
metadata.content: Warwickshire defeat Leicestershire at Edgbaston to win County Championship and claim first title in five years | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Warwickshire defeat Leicestershire at Edgbaston to win County Championship and claim first title in five years Warwickshire prove too good for Leicestershire at Edgbaston as the Bears win their first Rothesay County Championship since 2021 Saturday 26 September 2026 14:37, UK Image: Warwickshire players celebrate after beating Leicestershire by an innings to win the County Championship Division One title Warwickshire thrashed visitors Leicestershire by an innings and 79 runs at Edgbaston to seal a ninth County Championship title and their first since 2021 on Saturday. They entered the third day needing seven wickets to clinch the title, while the visitors needed 182 more runs to send them back in to bat. Chris Woakes got the hosts off to the ideal start by bowling Sol Budinger for 47 and the former England all-rounder soon struck again when his delivery to Jonathan Tattersall was caught by Rob Yates at slip.
